raw_response:
I will still start from what worked for me before. On 7.8 mu, I cannot gamble too much, because fertilizer, seed, pesticide, and water all cost money, and my family still has other expenses. I do not make a brand-new plan every year. I look at last year first, then I adjust a little. Around Quzhou, wheat-maize is still the steady way to keep grain coming, and with my well I do not want to leave that alone. But I also keep some cotton, because I have planted it many years and I know how to manage it. So this year I will keep about 5 mu in the wheat-maize rotation and 2.8 mu in cotton.

For wheat, I will not cut fertilizer too hard, because weak wheat in spring is hard to fix later. I will use improved wheat seed, give enough base fertilizer, and water about 3 times if the season is normal: once after sowing if dry, once at jointing, once at grain filling if needed. For maize, I will use hybrid seed, because the hybrids around here usually stand better and yield more if I feed them. I will not be stingy with nitrogen on maize, because if maize lacks fertilizer, the ears stay short. For cotton, I will keep the area smaller than grain land, but I will manage it carefully because cotton eats labor and pesticide money. I will give cotton more potassium than wheat and maize, because if bolls set poorly, I lose money fast. I will stay close to what nearby farmers do, and if I am unsure, I will do what has already worked on fields like mine rather than try something fancy.
